title: Score every pull on the rope
allegory: Direct logit attribution is like scoring a tug of war pull by pull: the rope runs from 'John' to 'Mary', every head pulls with its own arrow, and only the part of each pull along the rope counts, so the pulls add up exactly to the final result.
map: the rope, from John's flag to Mary's
the logit-difference direction W_U[:, IO] − W_U[:, S]
each component's output vector at the final position
the part of a pull along the rope
its dot product with that direction: a signed contribution
a negative name mover such as head 10.7
a coach who aims a puller but never touches the rope
an indirect effect, which DLA scores as zero

cap.1: The model finishes 'John gave a drink to...' with 'Mary'. GPT-2 small has 144 attention heads. Which ones actually pushed for Mary?
cap.2: You want per-component credit for one answer. Patching every head is slow, but there is a nearly free first pass, because the model's output is a sum.
cap.3: Goal: attribute logit[IO] − logit[S] to components. Exhaustive causal search is expensive; the residual stream's additivity gives an exact direct decomposition for free.

cap.1: Picture the answer as a tug of war between 'Mary' and 'John'. Every head grabs the rope and pulls: some for Mary, some for John, some just sideways.
cap.2: Each component writes a vector into the stream. Only the part of it along the 'Mary minus John' direction moves this answer. That part is its signed contribution.
cap.3: logit diff = x_final · (W_U[:, IO] − W_U[:, S]). Each component's term is its output dotted with that direction; orthogonal writes contribute nothing to this metric.

cap.1: Mary's lead is the sum of every pull along the rope. So each head's share is one number with a sign: for Mary or for John.
cap.2: Logit difference is linear in the residual stream, and the stream is a sum. Project each component's output onto the direction and the pieces add to the total.
cap.3: Linearity: (Σ fᵢ)·d = Σ (fᵢ·d), with d = W_U[:, IO] − W_U[:, S]. Logit difference is used rather than log-prob because a softmax would break the linearity.

chapters.name: The shortlist
chapters.title: Signed pull per head on IOI (signs from Wang et al.; sizes illustrative)

cap.1: Read off every head's pull and a few stand out. Heads 9.6 and 9.9 pull hard for Mary. Heads 10.7 and 11.10 pull hard the wrong way.
cap.2: On IOI in GPT-2 small, 144 heads collapse to a shortlist. The surprise was the negative heads: 10.7 and 11.10 push hard for the wrong name.
cap.3: Wang et al. (2022): name movers 9.6 and 9.9 are strongly positive; 10.7 and 11.10 are negative name movers, which no amount of staring at attention patterns would have suggested.

chapters.name: The shared referee

right.title: apply_ln_to_stack
lines: same cached scale on every piece
sums to the true logit diff

chapters.verdict: Freeze the final LayerNorm scale, then assert the pieces sum.

cap.1: At the end a referee shrinks every pull by the same amount. Forget that and your tallies rank right but never add up to the real score.
cap.2: ln_final divides the whole stream by one scale per position. Apply that cached scale to every component (cache.apply_ln_to_stack), then check the pieces sum to the logit difference.
cap.3: The LN scale is a nonlinear function of the full residual, so freeze the observed ln_final.hook_scale and apply it to each term. Skip it and every term shares one wrong factor.

cap.1: A coach who only tells a puller where to grab never touches the rope, so the tally gives the coach zero. DLA only sees who pulls directly.
cap.2: DLA measures direct paths to the logits only. A head whose job is to steer a later head's attention scores zero, like prev-token head 0.7 in the induction circuit.
cap.3: Effects mediated by later components (via Q, K or V composition) are invisible to DLA. Use it to shortlist, then path patching or activation patching for indirect effects.

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: Cheap first: shortlist heads with DLA
Some heads fight the model's own answer

cap.1: One cache, one projection, and you know who pushed the answer which way. It is the first move whenever you want to explain, or change, a behaviour.
cap.2: [1.4.1]'s workflow: DLA on the residual stack to shortlist heads, then patching to check them. Cheap first, expensive second. It is how you find what to steer or ablate.
cap.3: DLA gives an exact signed decomposition of a linear metric over direct paths. Pair it with causal methods for indirect effects before intervening on a model.

coda.title: Choose which answer you are scoring and watch each head's pull
coda.f: (() => { const W = [[2, 0.5], [1.5, -1], [-1.2, 0.8], [0.2, 1.5]]; const d = [Math.cos(th * PI / 180), Math.sin(th * PI / 180)]; const p = W.map(v => dot(v, d) / s); return p.concat([sum(p)]); })()

readouts.label: total write, projected once
readouts.f: (() => { const d = [Math.cos(th * PI / 180), Math.sin(th * PI / 180)]; return (dot([2.5, 1.8], d) / s).toFixed(2); })()

readouts.label: strongest puller
readouts.f: (() => { const d = [Math.cos(th * PI / 180), Math.sin(th * PI / 180)]; const p = [[2, 0.5], [1.5, -1], [-1.2, 0.8], [0.2, 1.5]].map(v => dot(v, d)); const i = p.map(Math.abs).indexOf(Math.max(...p.map(Math.abs))); return ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'][i] + (p[i] >= 0 ? ' (for)' : ' (against)'); })()

caption.1: Four heads each write an arrow. Turn the dial to choose which answer you are scoring; each bar is that head's pull. The total bar is always the sum.
caption.2: Contribution = the head's output dotted with the answer direction, divided by the LayerNorm scale. Change the direction and credit changes; change the scale and every bar shrinks together.
caption.3: DLA is metric-relative: creditᵢ = fᵢ·d / s. The sum identity holds for every d, and a shared s preserves the ranking, which is why skipping it misleads only in units.

where_else: The logit lens: the same projection applied to the whole stream at one layer
Direct feature attribution: the same trick with SAE features instead of heads
Linear probes: any linear readout of a sum splits across the sum's terms
Algorithmic-task interpretability, where DLA shortlists components in toy models

hamming.what: Splitting the model's answer, a logit difference, into one signed number per component by projecting each component's output onto the answer direction.
hamming.when: As the cheap first pass whenever you want to know which heads or layers produce a behaviour, before any patching.
hamming.why: The residual stream is a sum and the logit difference is linear, so the split is exact and costs a single cached forward pass.

object.title: The rope and the sheet
object.subtitle: Clouds of head outputs around a rope from John to Mary; a sheet holds every write that pulls sideways.

plane.label: writes here don't move Mary vs John

cap.1: Each cloud is one group of heads' writes over many prompts. The arrow is the Mary-versus-John rope.
cap.2: Head outputs as points; the arrow is W_U[:, Mary] − W_U[:, John].
cap.3: Per-head outputs at the final position across prompts; d = W_U[:, IO] − W_U[:, S].

cap.1: From the front, how far right or left a cloud sits is its pull for Mary or for John.
cap.2: Horizontal position = projection onto the answer direction = the DLA score.
cap.3: The x-coordinate is fᵢ·d/‖d‖: the signed direct contribution, up to scale.

cap.1: The sheet holds every write that pulls sideways: busy, but no help or harm to this answer.
cap.2: Writes in the plane perpendicular to the direction score zero, whatever else they do.
cap.3: Components writing in d⊥ have zero DLA for this metric but may matter for others.

cap.1: The surprising cloud: heads that push for the wrong name. DLA found them at once.
cap.2: Negative name movers 10.7 and 11.10 pull the logit difference down, towards the wrong name.
cap.3: Negative direct effects surfaced by DLA; Wang et al. (2022) named these negative name movers.

cap.1: What this picture cannot show: heads that only help others aim. They sit on the sheet and look useless.
cap.2: Indirect effects are invisible here; path patching finds them.
cap.3: DLA covers direct paths only; mediated effects need path patching or activation patching.

predict.q: A head writes a big vector perpendicular to the Mary-minus-John direction. Its DLA score?

options.t: Large, because the write is big

predict.why: Only the part of a write along the answer direction counts.

predict.q: Your head scores do not sum to the real logit difference. Likely fix?

options.t: Apply the final LayerNorm scale to every piece
Switch to log-probs instead of logits

predict.why: ln_final divides everything by one scale; apply it with apply_ln_to_stack and the pieces sum. Log-probs would break the linearity.

predict.q: Head 0.7 is essential for induction but scores zero on DLA. Why?

options.t: It only acts by steering later heads, an indirect path
DLA does not work on layer 0

predict.why: DLA sees only direct paths to the logits.
